document_or_genre: British Library Royal MS 12 G IV
attested_feature: An alphabetical herbal synonym list, a work on weights and measures with medicinal qualities, and Latin, French and English recipes coexist in one codex.
working_relevance: Supports the mixed architecture of learned substance names, productive quality stems, quantities and instruction blocks.
scope_limit: Architecture analogy only; it identifies no Voynich sign, language or ingredient.

attested_feature: Roughly 250 medical recipes, the Antidotarium Nicolai, a glossary of simples and herbs, and a De gradibus extract share the manuscript.
working_relevance: Near-period evidence that recipe instructions, degree tables and learned name glossaries can form one practical compilation.
scope_limit: Does not prove that the Voynich manuscript is this genre or uses the same vocabulary.

attested_feature: A botanical glossary and about 130 recipes accompany the Antidotarium Nicolai; catalogued recipe lines combine Recipe, drug names, dram signs and Roman quantities.
working_relevance: Supports compact take/measure commands beside whole drug names and explicit dose or portion values.
scope_limit: Does not map q, d, or, aiin or any other Voynich component.

attested_feature: The manuscript contains direct formulae of the form Recipe, named material, infuse in strong vinegar, and quantities such as equal amounts of two grains.
working_relevance: Supports a practical sequence of take, material, quantity, soaking or infusion, and prepared result.
scope_limit: Genre and syntax analogy only; no plaintext identification is claimed.

attested_feature: Liber graduum, Quid pro quo, medicinal recipes and an Arabic-Latin herbal-name glossary coexist.
working_relevance: Strong analogue for productive technical abbreviations used beside memorized or glossary-based whole names.
scope_limit: Does not select Arabic, Latin or any particular nomenclator for Voynichese.

document_or_genre: British Library Harley MS 2558, f.12v; Thomas Fayreford De saporibus et gradibus
attested_feature: A compact work on tastes and medicinal degrees was copied into a practical medical collection in the target period.
working_relevance: Supports hot, cold, dry and moist values combined with ordered degree notation around 1420.
scope_limit: Supports only the information type, not the proposed individual mappings.

document_or_genre: University of Nottingham palaeography guide to letter forms and abbreviations
attested_feature: Frequent words were heavily abbreviated, letters could be omitted, and minim sequences were context-dependent.
working_relevance: Makes joined and split alternatives such as chol ches, keo r, aiin dy and l karchees historically ordinary candidates for manual review.
scope_limit: Does not authorize arbitrary segmentation or identify rchr as a historical abbreviation.
